0e21a80a8c: Does ARGOS access real personal data?
b976a47392: Yes, during the discovery and classification phase, through read-only connectors. Everything happens inside your perimeter, with the model running locally and applying data minimisation: classifications and fingerprints are kept, not bulk copies of content. ARGOS's own access is logged and audited.
2e39c40129: Do synthetic subjects raise any data protection issue?
f5f70ca260: They are fictitious identities with plausible data that do not belong to any real person, so the tests create no risk for any data subject. When the campaign ends, ARGOS deletes them and verifies its own erasure.
b644720dc1: What happens when ARGOS detects a breach of the rules?
0659c58938: The finding is recorded with its evidence and verdict, enters the remediation plan and is notified to the internal roles you configure. ARGOS never reports anything to any authority or third party: that decision always belongs to the data controller.
8437ab16ce: Does the evidence carry weight with a data protection authority or an auditor?
001f1b1673: It is generated with a timestamp, a cryptographic chain of custody and the explicit evaluation rule, and the report is signed as a verifiable credential. It is complete and traceable; its assessment is for the authority or the auditor, who can check for themselves that it has not been altered.
805e8b51a5: If a verdict is wrong, who is accountable?
911761d85b: ARGOS is a support tool under human oversight. Each verdict references the exact rule and evidence, and decisions with legal effects are always taken by the compliance team: AI proposes, the engine disposes and the person decides.
1cd7899f30: Could ARGOS itself become a risk entry point?
e9a416dafa: It uses read-only connectors, has no outbound connection, receives signed one-way updates, is hardened to ENS high category and ISO 27001, and runs its own probes against itself.

3421fdb40b: The gap between declared and effective compliance
77a0b800ee: No authority fines you for what your documents say: it fines you for what your systems do. ARGOS measures and closes the gap between declared compliance (policies, records, contracts) and effective compliance (what systems really do with data), turning it into actionable findings backed by evidence.
850c931ac8: ARGOS does not observe passively: it challenges. It launches controlled tests against real systems —access requests, erasure orders, flow traces— and checks whether the response is what the regulation requires. Seven families of probes cover the full data life cycle.
3d8e192ad0: A synthetic subject is a fictitious but technically complete identity that ARGOS injects into systems as a tracer. It is not a real person —there is no risk to anyone— but it travels the same paths as real data, making it possible to verify access, transfers and erasure end to end.
54779ae079: ARGOS delivers four things: a live inventory of systems and data, compliance verdicts with traceable technical evidence, a continuous dashboard for the DPO and management, and the verifiable credential that proves compliance to third parties without exposing anything.
a01b4b0f37: Three clocks are ticking at once: the AI Act has applied since 2 August 2026 and its high-risk obligations arrive on 2 December 2027 (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744), the EHDS rolls out its timetable until 2035, and GDPR fines have topped €5.88 billion since 2018. Continuous verification is no longer optional.
839b4e0d4e: Seven functional layers: C0 evidence and credentials (Auditree, XFSC, W3C VC), C1 regulatory catalogue (OSCAL, ODRL), C2 data discovery (OpenMetadata, Presidio), C3 agent orchestration (LangGraph, MCP), C4 the challenge module with its seven families of probes, C5 the deterministic decision engine (OPA/Rego) and C6 reports and dashboard.
86efb1c491: The guiding principle: AI proposes, the engine disposes. The local language model interprets, plans and drafts, but no compliance verdict comes from it: verdicts are issued by a deterministic rules engine (OPA/Rego) evaluating technical evidence. A hallucination cannot become a verdict.
5fcd3115a2: Every verdict is traceable end to end through the chain regulation → obligation → control → evidence → verdict. Before an auditor or an authority, any ARGOS conclusion can be unfolded down to the specific article that requires it and the technical evidence that supports it.
d8dff8c076: Yes: it is one of the flagship checks. After an erasure order, the erasure probe re-inspects every repository where the data appeared —primaries, replicas, indexes, accessible backups— and if the data persists in any of them, it is recorded as a finding with evidence.
8c5727c5fb: Every piece of evidence is sealed with SHA-256 in an append-only chain: nothing can be altered without breaking the chain. On that foundation, ARGOS issues W3C verifiable credentials validated through Gaia-X (GXDCH): compliance that can be demonstrated to third parties without exposing a single piece of data from the perimeter.
2cc0a16e1f: Nothing. ARGOS is an on-premise appliance with no outbound connection: no telemetry, no cloud, no dependence on an external provider. The AI model runs locally and the connectors are read-only. The only thing that can leave, if you so decide, is a signed, one-way package: the credential.

2a49496cf4: The cycle of a verification campaign
0dc95a6636: how it works day to day
9a90bc1e45: Each campaign follows a closed cycle: planning from the regulatory catalogue, running probes against the systems, capturing and sealing evidence, verdicts from the deterministic engine, a report with prioritised findings, and remediation verified by a new probe. Then it starts again: continuous verification.
8c719de1c3: A finding is not closed because someone says they have fixed it: it is closed when a new probe verifies that the fix works. If re-verification fails, the finding is automatically reopened. The same philosophy as always: verified, not declared.
5402a24087: The catalogue covers the European and Spanish core of data protection and governance: GDPR and LOPDGDD, EHDS, AI Act, ENS, NIS2, Data Act and Data Governance Act, with sector profiles that activate the rules applicable to each organisation.
eeb8d74ed9: The EHDS Regulation (EU) 2025/327 has been in force since 26 March 2025, with general application on 26 March 2027 and phased obligations until 2035. For the health sector, traceability of access to clinical data stops being good practice and becomes a verifiable obligation.
56ef5e7bc1: High-risk AI systems: from census to evidence
c40183231e: First, the census: ARGOS surfaces the real AI systems —including shadow AI— and classifies them against the areas of Annex III. Then comes the technical verification of the high-risk obligations, enforceable from 2 December 2027: event logging (Art. 12), transparency (Art. 13) and human oversight (Art. 14), among others.
798bcf9f53: Overlapping regulations, turned into an advantage
c61adbd1e0: A single piece of evidence produces simultaneous verdicts across all the regulations in the profile: the same access log feeds the GDPR, the EHDS, the ENS and NIS2 at once, because each control in the catalogue is linked to every obligation that requires it. One campaign, readings for every regulation.
b71240314e: A data breach: 72 hours to notify
17cb806ca6: After a breach, Article 33 of the GDPR gives you 72 hours to notify. Without a live inventory, those hours are spent reconstructing which systems and which data exist. With ARGOS, the inventory answers in hours and the evidence chain documents the state of the controls before the incident: due diligence is demonstrated.
3c8effb023: ARGOS and your GRC platform: they do not compete
0a06264228: They do not compete: GRC governs, ARGOS proves. Your GRC platform organises policies, risks and workflows, but its evidence is declarative. ARGOS adds the missing layer —technical evidence of how data really behaves— and integrates it via API into the controls of your existing GRC.
